newsitem.title: USA: Mexico drugs talks continue in U.S. Senate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico drugs talks continue in U.S. Senate.

text.p: Aides to key senators continued Tuesday to try to draft a measure signifying congressional discontent with Mexico's perceived failure to deal with drug trafficking to the United States.
"A lot of progress has been made. We are moving forward," a Senate aide said.

High Clinton administration officials, led by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, presented proposals to the senators Monday night. The administration is seeking to head off a Senate move to overturn President Clinton's certification of Mexico as fully cooperating in the anti-drug war.

Three senators are trying to work out a compromise resolution expected to be acted upon this week that would register congressional dissatisfaction with Mexico without torpedoing current cooperation between the two countries.

Sens Paul Coverdell, a Georgia Republican, and Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat, have proposed "decertification" with a waiver of sanctions against Mexico while Texas Republican Kay Bailey Hutchison has proposed a non-binding resolution expressing congressional views.
